  • Own the end-to-end design and execution of marketing-led HCP education and P2P programs, including speaker programs, Peer Discussion Groups, ITUs, and other approved customer education opportunities.

  • Lead speaker training and development strategy, including curriculum design, content readiness, faculty preparation, and ongoing capability building for new and tenured speakers.

  • Partner with Sales Training and field leadership to strengthen field readiness, appropriate program pull-through, and a consistent customer experience.

Lead Opinion Leader Engagement at Congresses

  • Own all marketing-led OL-facing engagement at congresses, including ITUs, symposia, product theaters, speaker and faculty activity, and other approved OL-present programs.

  • Set the strategy, objectives, and engagement plans for the OL-facing congress workstream; lead and direct the team members responsible for detailed planning and on-site pull-through.

  • Partner with the TLL team to identify and coordinate priority OL engagements for the Neuro Medical Marketing Lead, other leaders, and cross-functional partners before and during congresses; ensure agreed follow-up actions are completed after the event.

  • Partner with the Insights & Congress Strategy lead to integrate OL engagement plans into sponsorship choices, the broader congress activation strategy, and post-congress learning. Partner with Professional Marketing to align OL-facing programs with its booth-related and sales-driven assets.

Build Content and Deliver High-Quality Execution

  • Own development and lifecycle management of P2P materials, including speaker decks, disease-state resources, case-based materials, and program tools; oversee agency development, MAC review, approval, rollout, and updates.

  • Ensure P2P content and speaker training clearly communicate the scientific and clinical rationale for UPLIZNA while meeting the distinct needs of gMG and NMOSD customers.

  • Manage P2P and OL engagement budgets, agencies, and external vendors with strong financial stewardship, rigorous prioritization, and accountability for timely, high-quality delivery.

  • Ensure high-quality execution across the portfolio by setting clear operating models, timelines, decision rights, and standards for program planning, vendor management, compliance, and follow-up.

Drive Performance, Insights, and Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Define and monitor meaningful measures of P2P, Speaker Bureau, and OL engagement performance, including program quality, reach, utilization, speaker effectiveness, audience feedback, and strategic impact.

  • Translate field feedback, customer insights, program data, competitive intelligence, and external engagement learnings into clear recommendations to improve OL engagement strategy, P2P content, and execution.

  • Contribute to annual brand planning, long-range planning, quarterly priorities, and tactical plans by bringing forward customer, scientific, and performance implications.

  • Represent OL Engagement and P2P Medical Marketing in key franchise forums and communicate performance, emerging risks, opportunities, and recommendations to senior leadership.

Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

  • Directly lead, coach, and develop team members responsible for P2P execution and related Medical Marketing workstreams; establish clear priorities, decision rights, accountability, and development plans.

  • Create an operating model that balances strategic leadership with disciplined execution, enabling the team to manage complex workstreams while maintaining a strong customer and business focus.

  • Foster a culture of scientific curiosity, customer centricity, ownership, collaboration, innovation, and high standards of execution. Live and role model Amgen Values across the UPLIZNA brand team and cross-functional partners.

Win

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The strategic professional we seek is a motivated individual with these qualifications.

  • Doctorate degree and 2 years of marketing and/or business experience in a role aligned with a Marketing/Sales commercial organization; OR

  • Master's degree and 4 years of marketing and/or business experience in a role aligned with a Marketing/Sales commercial organization; OR

  • Bachelor's degree and 6 years of marketing and/or business experience in a role aligned with a Marketing/Sales commercial organization; OR

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated direct people-management experience, including coaching and developing talent, setting priorities, and leading through change.

  • Strong Medical Marketing, OL engagement, and P2P expertise, including OL mapping and engagement planning, Speaker Bureau operations, speaker training, marketing-led HCP education, promotional content development, and multichannel education.

  • Neurology experience preferred; rare disease and launch or in-line brand experience preferred.

Thrive

What you can expect from us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

This role is responsible for reviewing case files ahead of scheduled depositions to identify opportunities for resolution prior to deposition, preparing deposition strategy and questions, and appearing at and conducting QME depositions — both applicant-set and defense-set — to develop the record and advance the client's position. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable working independently under deadline pressure in a fast-paced workers' compensation litigation environment.

Key Responsibilities

Pre-Deposition Case Review

  • Review assigned case files in advance of each scheduled QME deposition to assess case status, medical-legal issues, and litigation posture.
  • Evaluate whether resolution (settlement, stipulation) is achievable prior to the deposition date, and discuss viable cases with the adjuster or client.
  • Communicate with attorneys, adjusters, and opposing counsel to explore early resolution options and confirm whether a deposition can be avoided, continued, or must proceed.
  • Document case review findings and resolution recommendations in the case management system.

Deposition Preparation

  • Review the case file in depth prior to the QME deposition, including claim history, prior medical treatment records, and the QME/AME report(s), to identify key factual and medical issues.
  • Analyze the QME report(s) for internal inconsistencies, gaps, causation issues, apportionment concerns, or areas that need clarification through testimony.
  • Identify disputed issues (e.g., AOE/COE, body parts, permanent disability, need for further treatment, apportionment) and determine what the deposition needs to establish or challenge.
  • Contact the client as needed to get an updated sense of their current medical status, ongoing symptoms, treatment, and how their case is progressing, to make sure the questions and strategy reflect where things stand.

Deposition Attendance

  • Appear at and conduct QME depositions — both applicant-set and defense-set — in person or remotely, questioning the QME and making appropriate objections on the record.
  • Take detailed notes during depositions, tracking key testimony, exhibits marked, and outstanding issues.
  • Manage exhibits and make real-time strategic decisions on the scope and direction of questioning during the deposition.
  • Coordinate post-deposition follow-up tasks.

Administrative & Case Management

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date case files, deposition logs, and status reports.
  • Communicate proactively with internal team members regarding case status, resolution opportunities, and deposition outcomes.
  • Perform other litigation duties as assigned.
  • Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree and active license to practice law in California (active member of the State Bar of California) required.
  • 1+ years of experience litigating workers' compensation cases, including taking QME/AME depositions, strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of California workers' compensation procedures, QME processes, and deposition practice (or willingness to learn quickly).
  • Prior experience as an associate attorney in a workers' compensation defense or applicant firm is a plus.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to assess case files and identify resolution opportunities.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Highly organized with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple deposition schedules simultaneously.

  • Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and meet firm deadlines.

  • Proficiency with case management software, Microsoft Office (Word, Outlook, Excel), and e-filing/e-service systems.

  • Professional demeanor and courtroom-appropriate presence suitable for examining medical evaluators and appearing opposite opposing counsel.

Work Environment

  • May require occasional early morning, evening, or extended hours to accommodate deposition schedules.

Background

CLEAR Global is a nonprofit organization helping people get vital information and be heard, whatever language they speak. As part of this mission, CLEAR Global maintains the Language Use Data Platform (LUDP), a data platform that aggregates and standardizes language and geographic data to support humanitarian and language-access initiatives globally.

As LUDP expands into additional countries and languages, CLEAR Global is piloting and refining workflows for identifying, processing, validating, and publishing multilingual datasets. This internship will support the testing and documentation of these operational processes to help ensure they are scalable, accurate, and sustainable.

Objectives

The objective of this internship is to support a pilot implementation of the “Adding a Country” workflow for LUDP. The intern will help test and document the feasibility, clarity, and timing of the process by working through real country-level language datasets and supporting data preparation, validation, and reporting activities.

The role

The MIIS Intern will support the LUDP Team in piloting workflows related to language dataset acquisition, processing, quality assurance, and publication. Working closely with CLEAR Global staff, the intern will contribute to testing operational procedures, documenting findings, identifying gaps or inefficiencies, and helping improve internal guidance and processes for future country expansion efforts.

Responsibilities

  • Support the identification and acquisition of country-level language datasets from public and institutional sources.
  • Prepare and standardize datasets for integration into the LUDP environment.
  • Assist with data cleaning, formatting, and metadata verification.
  • Run and document data processing workflows using existing tools and templates.
  • Support quality assurance and validation activities, including cross-referencing linguistic and geographic information.
  • Document workflow challenges, ambiguities, timing estimates, and process improvement recommendations.
  • Assist in drafting update reports and maintaining process documentation.
  • Collaborate with CLEAR Global staff to refine operational guidance and workflow materials.
  • Undertake other quality operations tasks as assigned.
  • Act in the best interest of the organization during the project period.

These roles and responsibilities are approximate and may change over time.

Qualifications

  • Strong organizational and analytical skills.
  • Attention to detail and ability to follow structured processes.
  • Comfort working with spreadsheets and structured datasets.
  • Interest in language data, multilingual technology, humanitarian technology, or localization workflows.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.
  • Strong written and spoken English.

Requirements

This position is very dynamic. The right person is an energetic team player who agrees with CLEAR Global’s basic beliefs and values and can work remotely while interacting regularly with the international team.

  • Self-starter;
  • Strong organizational skills;
  • Analytical thinker able to transform ideas into tangible actions;
  • Understands that communication in the right language is key to improved humanitarian response;
  • Team player, collaborative, adaptable and self-motivated;
  • Interest in acquiring translation project management experience;
  • Ability to adapt to new technologies and learn new skills quickly;
  • Attention to detail.

About CLEAR Global

CLEAR Global exists to help people get vital information, and be heard, whatever language they speak. We believe that everyone has the right to give and receive information in a language and format they understand. We work with nonprofit partners and a global community of language professionals to build local language translation capacity, and raise awareness of language barriers. Our network of over 200,000 community members translate millions of words of life-saving and life-changing information a year.

Core values

CLEAR Global employees and volunteers are people who believe passionately about the value of this work and take personal responsibility for achieving the mission. CLEAR Global’s mission and organizational spirit embody the core values established in its strategic framework:

  • Excellence: As the leading voice for communicating humanitarian information in the right language, CLEAR Global is a leader in the translation industry and in the non-profit sector.
  • Integrity: CLEAR Global believes that every person, whether it’s the people who we serve, our volunteers or our staff, has value, deserves respect and has inherent dignity.
  • Empowerment: CLEAR Global believes in using language to empower people around the world to control their own development and destiny.
  • Innovation: CLEAR Global recognizes and celebrates the power of innovation to address humanitarian and crisis issues around the world.
  • Sustainability: CLEAR Global recognizes that meeting our mission necessitates establishment and maintenance of a solid financial and organizational infrastructure.
  • Tolerance: Our staff and volunteers are highly knowledgeable and skilled; value each other, our partner and our recipients; create a supportive work environment; and conduct themselves professionally at all times.

Clearance

Public Trust

Overview

Ardent Eagle Solutions (AES) is seeking Records Management Specialists to support a competitive federal contracting opportunity with the U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), Economic Development Administration (EDA).

The Records Management Specialist will support the assessment, modernization, and ongoing execution of EDA's Records Management Program. Working alongside senior records management personnel and Government stakeholders, this position will assist with records inventories, audits, electronic records management, document control, disposition activities, administrative procedures, program documentation, and records management training and sustainment efforts.

Background

EDA requires contractor support to strengthen and standardize records management practices across its Headquarters and six regional offices. The program is intended to improve records inventories and disposition processes, digital and email records controls, process documentation, training, and the overall consistency and sustainability of EDA's Records Management Program.

The work will support a broader effort to establish practical, repeatable records management processes and transfer usable tools and resources to Government personnel.

Responsibilities

The Records Management Specialist is expected to:

  • Support Senior Records Managers in assessing, redesigning, and executing EDA's Records Management Program.
  • Assist with the analysis, development, and review of administrative operating procedures.
  • Support records management activities, management plans, reports, and program documentation.
  • Participate in records inventories, audits, and reconciliations.
  • Identify and document records series, owners, formats, volumes, locations, restrictions, and applicable records schedules.
  • Coordinate and track document requests in accordance with applicable NARA and Federal Records Center guidance.
  • Support classification reviews, as required.
  • Respond to customer requests for records, documents, or records management assistance.
  • Digitize analog records into electronic formats in accordance with applicable NARA standards.
  • Support preparation of expired records for authorized destruction or other disposition.
  • Perform records receipt, storage, indexing, and inventory activities.
  • Conduct quality control reviews of records and box contents.
  • Perform inventory reconciliations and assist with identifying discrepancies or corrective actions.
  • Support digital and electronic records activities involving email, electronic messages, shared drives, SharePoint, and other repositories.
  • Assist in developing SOPs, desk guides, checklists, training materials, and other records management resources.
  • Coordinate schedules for deliverables, reviews, briefings, and other program activities.
  • Assist with progress reporting, transition activities, and knowledge transfer.
  • Collaborate with geographically dispersed Government and contractor personnel to support consistent records management practices across EDA.

Qualifications

Approximately 4 or more years of related professional experience in records management, document management, information management, information governance, administrative records support, or a closely related field.

  • Experience working with NARA records retention policies, schedules, or records management requirements.
  • Experience supporting records inventories, file plans, records disposition, document control, indexing, digitization, or records reconciliation activities.
  • Familiarity with electronic records and common digital repositories, such as shared drives, SharePoint, email systems, or comparable platforms.
  • Ability to organize, track, review, and reconcile large volumes of records or information accurately.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality control.
  • Ability to interpret established policies and procedures and apply them consistently.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with senior records management personnel, Government stakeholders, and geographically dispersed teams.
  • Prior federal records management or federal contracting experience is preferred.

Education

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.

Location and Work Hours

This position is expected to be primarily remote and may be performed from locations throughout the United States, subject to final contract requirements and Government approval.

Although this requisition may be advertised using Washington, D.C. as the posting location, candidates are not expected to reside in the Washington metropolitan area solely because of the posting location.

The position will support EDA Headquarters and/or one or more regional offices located in Philadelphia, Atlanta, Chicago, Austin, Denver, and Seattle. Current contract documentation anticipates primarily remote performance with onsite support when appropriately authorized.

Normal work hours are expected to be Monday through Friday during standard business hours, excluding Federal holidays and Government-directed closures.

Travel

Approximately 10% travel is anticipated based on current planning assumptions. Travel may include authorized visits to EDA Headquarters or regional offices to support inventories, assessments, meetings, records activities, training, or other program requirements.

Compensation

Anticipated Salary Range: $60,000- $70,000 annually

This position is being recruited in support of a competitive federal contracting opportunity, and AES is continuing to develop its staffing, labor category, and compensation strategy. Because this position is expected to support a primarily remote workforce and qualified candidates may reside in different geographic markets throughout the United States, compensation expectations may vary considerably by location.

Final compensation will consider factors including geographic market, relevant experience, education, specialized records management expertise, applicable labor category requirements, and contractual and business considerations.

AES welcomes open and collaborative compensation discussions with interested candidates as we evaluate the market and develop an accurate and competitive compensation strategy for this opportunity. The range above represents our current anticipated range and is not a guarantee of a specific salary or compensation level.

This is a remote position.

The Product Lead Engineer serves as the technical authority across multiple Agile scrum teams inside a vertical product. This role carries no personnel management responsibilities but holds the highest technical voice within the team — setting direction, making implementation calls, and ensuring the team delivers reliable, well-engineered software. Beyond their own contributions, the Product Lead Engineer's output raises the technical capability of everyone around them.

Core Responsibilities

Technical Team Leadership

  • Serve as the technical authority within the development teams — making implementation decisions, resolving technical disagreements, and ensuring the team operates to a consistently high engineering standard.
  • Lead end-to-end delivery of complex features across backend, frontend, and mobile platforms — from design through deployment and monitoring — while actively guiding teammates through their portions of the work.
  • Decompose ambiguous requirements into well-scoped tasks; proactively identify and address technical debt, performance bottlenecks, and reliability risks.
  • Regularly and actively contribute production code (player-coach role) as a consistent, high-quality committer who models the engineering standards the rest of the organization is held to.

Technical Leadership & Mentorship

  • Conduct thorough, constructive code reviews that improve quality and accelerate the growth of junior engineers.
  • Mentor Software Engineers through pairing, design discussions, and regular technical guidance.
  • Drive best practices for testing, branching, documentation, and security within the team.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with Product, QA, and Customer Success to clarify requirements, estimate accurately, and deliver reliable features on schedule.
  • Communicate clearly and proactively about technical risks, progress, and tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Technical Ownership & Cross-Training

  • Take primary ownership of one or more significant product areas — maintaining deep expertise in their architecture, behavior, and failure modes — and serve as the authoritative resource for decisions and issues in those areas.
  • Proactively lead knowledge transfer of owned areas to teammates so the team can operate effectively without any single engineer becoming a bottleneck.
  • Actively participate in cross-training led by others, developing meaningful familiarity with product areas outside primary ownership to strengthen overall team resilience.

Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of professional software development experience, including production SaaS environments.
  • Deep proficiency in PHP and JavaScript / React, including design patterns, performance, and security best practices.
  • Strong command of relational database design, SQL optimization, and data modeling (MySQL / MariaDB).
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor and upskill less experienced engineers.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted engineering tooling and workflows.

  • Develop and validate steady state models in ETAP and PSSE, and dynamic models in PSS®E and PSCAD for:

    • Large electronic loads (e.g., data centers)

    • PV, wind, and BESS resources

  • Support development and integration of:

    • Solar/Wind/BESS Power Plant Controllers (PPCs)

    • Master Plant Controllers (MPCs)

  • Participate in EPC HV/MV substation design studies for:

    • Large data center projects

  • Support or lead microgrid design and control studies at MV and HV levels.

  • Support RTDS / RSCAD CHIL testing (Control Hardware-in-the-Loop).

  • Interface with Transmission Service Providers (TSPs), ISO/RTOs (especially ERCOT), developers, OEMs, and project stakeholders.

  • Perform steady-state and short-circuit analyses including: Load flow studies, Short circuit analysis, Protection coordination, Arc-flash studies, Reactive power and energy loss analysis, and Harmonic studies

  • Conduct electromagnetic transient (EMT) studies in PSCAD, including: Transient overvoltage (TOV), Transient recovery voltage (TRV), Insulation coordination, SSR/SSO screening and mitigation analysis

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering (Power Systems preferred).

  • 8+ years of relevant experience in power systems planning and interconnection.

  • Strong experience in:

  • Demonstrated experience with:

    • Large load interconnection studies (data center experience strongly preferred)

    • ERCOT transmission planning and compliance requirements

    • Generation interconnection (PV, wind, BESS)

From airplane engines to hydraulic systems, scotch to smartphones, OLED screens to paper—everyday Pall is there, helping protect critical operating assets, improve product quality, minimize emissions and waste, and safeguard health. For the exponentially curious, Pall is a place where you can thrive and amplify your impact on the world. jobs.title: HR People & Culture Specialists | Poppy & Peonies
jobs.excerpt: Bloom is a full-service workplace design consultancy proudly supporting Poppy & Peonies in its search for an HR People & Culture Specialists.
jobs.description:
Bloom is a full-service workplace design consultancy proudly supporting Poppy & Peonies in its search for an HR People & Culture Specialists. As Talent Advisors, we’ll be your point of contact throughout the recruitment process. Every application is reviewed by a real person, and if selected, you’ll join Poppy & Peonies directly as a valued member of their team. We’re excited to consider your application!

Meet Poppy & Peonies

Hi, I’m Natalie Dusome, Founder and CEO of Poppy & Peonies.

At Poppy & Peonies, we’re a fun and energetic brand that believes style and function should always go hand in hand.

Our story began in 2015 after my daughter, Poppy, was born. I realized that the accessories I owned no longer worked for my life as a mom. I needed bags with pockets and organization that were practical without sacrificing style. When I couldn’t find them, I decided to create them myself.

Since then, we’ve grown from filling orders in my basement to appearing on Dragons’ Den, expanding into new product categories, and collaborating with exciting influencers and brands. It hasn’t always been smooth sailing, but thanks to our incredible team and community, we’ve never felt more loved or supported.

We also believe we have a responsibility to care for the environment and protect the health and welfare of our planet and its animals. Our bags are made from high-quality vegan leather, and our entire product line is vegan, cruelty-free, and PETA-approved. We ship our products plastic-free and use recycled, compostable, and biodegradable materials wherever possible. We’re continually looking for ways to make our products and supply chain more sustainable.

The Role:

    As our HR People & Culture Specialists, you’ll lead the day-to-day people function at Poppy & Peonies while helping us build the programs, practices, and infrastructure required for our next stage of growth.

    This is a broad, hands-on HR and Generalist role. You’ll be responsible for the core employee lifecycle, including onboarding, performance management, benefits, employee relations, engagement, learning and development, policy administration, and offboarding. You’ll also oversee the culture and employee experience work that helps our remote-first team feel connected, supported, and part of something meaningful.

    You’ll partner closely with our founder and leadership team to translate business priorities into practical people plans. You’ll help leaders anticipate what the team will need, identify gaps before they become larger problems, and scale the strong HR programs and systems already in place.

    This is an intermediate-level opportunity for someone who can operate independently and provide trusted guidance while remaining willing to roll up their sleeves. You won’t be joining a large HR department with highly specialized roles. You’ll need to move comfortably between planning, advising, problem-solving, program management, and detailed execution.

    Success in this role requires an understanding of how founder-led companies operate. You’ll know how to build a trusted partnership with a founder, introduce the right level of structure without creating unnecessary bureaucracy, and support a growing team through change while remaining grounded in thoughtful, consistent HR practices.

The Opportunity:

    HR Partnership and People Planning

  • Partner with the founder and leadership team to understand business priorities and translate them into practical people plans.
  • Develop short- and longer-term workforce plans that consider organizational growth, team capacity, critical roles, succession needs, and emerging skill gaps.
  • Provide leaders with clear, thoughtful HR guidance grounded in company values, employment practices, and business realities.
  • Use employee feedback, workforce data, and organizational observations to identify risks, patterns, and opportunities.
  • Support organizational design, role clarity, reporting relationships, and evolving team structures.
  • Help leaders assess the people impact of business decisions and plan effectively for periods of growth or change.
  • Establish meaningful people metrics and provide leadership with useful insights and recommendations.
  • Partner with external HR and legal advisors when specialized guidance is required.

    • Manager Support and Performance

  • Lead and continually improve the company’s performance management approach, including goal setting, feedback, performance reviews, development planning, and performance improvement.
  • Coach managers through performance concerns, difficult conversations, team dynamics, role clarity, and employee development.
  • Equip new and existing managers with practical tools, resources, and training to lead effectively.
  • Help managers establish clear expectations, address concerns promptly, and document performance matters appropriately.
  • Support the development of high-performing teams by strengthening accountability, communication, and feedback practices.
  • Identify recurring manager needs and develop scalable programming, resources, or training in response.
  • Guide leaders through promotions, compensation decisions, internal transitions, and role changes.

    • Employee Relations and HR Operations

  • Serve as a trusted point of contact for employees and managers seeking HR guidance or support.
  • Manage employee relations matters with care, discretion, consistency, and sound judgment.
  • Lead workplace investigations or coordinate external support when appropriate.
  • Manage accommodations, leaves, attendance concerns, performance matters, and other employee-related processes.
  • Maintain accurate employee records, documentation, templates, and HR systems.
  • Develop, review, and administer workplace policies and procedures.
  • Monitor evolving employment standards and HR requirements, escalating complex legal matters when necessary.
  • Support compensation administration and help maintain equitable and consistent compensation practices.
  • Manage employee benefits administration, including enrolment, employee questions, renewals, and relationships with external providers.
  • Lead respectful and well-organized offboarding processes, including terminations, resignations, documentation, and exit feedback.
  • Protect employee confidentiality while maintaining appropriate communication and documentation across the organization.

    • Culture and Employee Experience

  • Own and continually evaluate the employee experience across the full employee lifecycle.
  • Oversee onboarding so every new employee feels welcomed, informed, prepared, and connected from the beginning.
  • Develop and coordinate culture-building programs, team rituals, recognition initiatives, virtual events, celebrations, and opportunities for meaningful connection.
  • Translate Poppy & Peonies’ values into clear and consistent employee experiences, programs, and leadership practices.
  • Lead employee listening initiatives, including surveys, check-ins, focus groups, and other feedback channels.
  • Turn employee feedback into practical recommendations and ensure agreed-upon actions are followed through.
  • Support internal communications related to people programs, organizational changes, company initiatives, and team milestones.
  • Develop learning and development programming for employees and managers.
  • Track participation, feedback, and outcomes to understand which programs are working and where improvements are needed.
  • Oversee the work of the Culture Specialist, providing direction, support, prioritization, and accountability.

    • Recruitment and Workforce Growth

  • Partner with leaders to define hiring priorities, workforce needs, role requirements, and realistic recruitment timelines.
  • Manage relationships with Bloom and other external recruitment partners, ensuring vendors have clear direction and deliver a thoughtful candidate experience.
  • Review and improve job descriptions, hiring processes, interview practices, and candidate communications.
  • Support managers in making consistent, evidence-based hiring decisions.
  • Ensure recruitment and selection practices are equitable, accessible, and aligned with Poppy & Peonies’ values.
  • Monitor recruitment progress, hiring outcomes, vendor performance, and associated costs.
  • Lead the transition from recruitment into onboarding so new employees have a consistent experience from offer acceptance through their first months with the company.
  • Help determine when recruitment should be handled internally and when external support is the best approach.

    • Programs, Systems, and Scale

  • Assess existing HR programs and systems to determine what should be strengthened, simplified, or scaled.
  • Build sustainable processes appropriate for a small but growing company.
  • Create clear workflows, templates, playbooks, and resources that make it easier for employees and managers to navigate HR processes.
  • Ensure people programs remain consistent while allowing for the flexibility required in an entrepreneurial environment.
  • Lead the implementation or improvement of HR technology and people-related tools.
  • Maintain an organized annual people calendar covering performance, compensation, benefits, engagement, learning, policy reviews, and other recurring priorities.
  • Balance immediate employee and operational needs with the longer-term work required to strengthen the people function.

What you bring to the table:

  • Approximately 5–7 years of progressive HR experience, including meaningful generalist responsibility.
  • Experience operating at an HR Manager, Senior HR Generalist, People Operations Manager, or comparable intermediate level.
  • Experience supporting a small but scaling company where priorities, roles, and processes continue to evolve.
  • Experience working directly with a founder and senior leaders in a founder-led business.
  • Strong generalist knowledge across performance management, employee relations, benefits, policies, onboarding, employee experience, learning and development, and offboarding.
  • Experience coaching managers through performance concerns, feedback conversations, team challenges, and employee development.
  • Experience developing, improving, and scaling people programs, processes, and systems.
  • The ability to move between strategic planning and detailed execution without losing momentum on either.
  • Strong judgment and the ability to distinguish between issues you can manage independently and those requiring legal or specialized guidance.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to make complex or sensitive information clear.
  • Strong relationship-building skills and the confidence to provide candid, respectful guidance to founders and leaders.
  • Excellent organization, project management, and follow-through.
  • Comfort handling confidential and sensitive employee information.
  • Experience supporting remote-first or distributed teams.
  • Working knowledge of applicable Canadian employment standards and HR practices; experience supporting employees across multiple provinces or jurisdictions is an asset.
  • A relevant post-secondary qualification or HR designation is an asset but not required where equivalent experience is demonstrated.
  • Experience within e-commerce, retail, consumer goods, fashion, or another fast-moving customer-focused environment is a bonus.

    • Don’t sweat it if you don’t have everything listed above. We believe in growth and curiosity. If you bring many of these qualities and are excited about the opportunity, we want to hear from you!

The Recruitment Process:

  • Video screen with Niamh, Talent Advisor at Bloom
  • Video interview with Nat Bates
  • Final video interview with Nat Dusome
  • Reference checks
  • Offer

Location:

    We’re a fully remote team spread across North America, which means you can work from wherever you do your best thinking, collaborating, and problem-solving. While this role is fully remote, there may be opportunities for domestic or international travel for team gatherings, special events, and the occasional chance to connect in person.

Salary and Total Rewards:

  • Salary range: $95,000–$110,000 CAD annually
  • 15 days of paid vacation
  • Health benefits coverage
  • $250 annual period and menstrual budget
  • $1,000 annual allowance toward Poppy & Peonies products
  • $400 home office setup allowance
    • All compensation and benefit amounts are reflected in local currency (CAD/USD where applicable).
    At Bloom, we see conversations around compensation as a continuous discussion. We encourage you to share your desired compensation early in the interview process, but we also understand that as you learn more about the role and the full benefits package, your expectations might evolve. Don't worry - there will be plenty of opportunities throughout the process to revisit and adjust those conversations if needed.

Our Commitment to you.

Like Bloom, Poppy & Peonies is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We are committed to equitable employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or veteran status.

We’re looking for motivated, compassionate people who are excited to contribute, grow with the team, and support the values that Poppy & Peonies believes in.

Poppy & Peonies is committed to developing an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment process and work environment. Please inform us if you require any accommodation, and we will work with you to meet your accessibility needs. Requests for any accessibility-related assistance can be made to

believe transparency matters, especially as technology evolves.

At Bloom, we may leverage AI as a supportive tool when developing role descriptions, interview questions, take home assignments, and interview guides, where appropriate, with the goal of improving clarity, consistency, and accessibility for candidates. However, we do not use AI to source, assess, screen, or interview candidates. Every application is reviewed by a human, every interview is conducted by a human, and all hiring decisions are made by people, not automated systems. Human judgment, care, and accountability are central to how we hire.

About Bloom

Bloom is a full-service workplace design consultancy representing Poppy & Peonies at they build their team. As Talent Advisors, we will be the liaison between our Bloom Partner and yourself during this recruitment process. We do not use fancy tech to search through resumes at Bloom; every resume is reviewed by a human to ensure that we attain a consistent and equitable interview process. You will directly join our client’s team if you are selected as the successful candidate. We look forward to seeing your application!

jobs.excerpt: Job FamilyTaxAbout Us At Transamerica, hard work, innovative thinking, and personal accountability are qualities we honor and reward.
jobs.description:
Job Family

Tax

About Us

At Transamerica, hard work, innovative thinking, and personal accountability are qualities we honor and reward. We understand the potential of leveraging the talents of a diverse workforce. We embrace an environment where employees enjoy a balance between their careers, families, communities, and personal interests.

Ultimately, we appreciate the uniqueness of a company where talented professionals work collaboratively in a positive environment — one focused on helping people look forward and plan for the best life possible while providing tools and solutions that make it easier to get there.

   

Who We Are

 

We believe everyone deserves to live their best life. More than a century ago, we were among the first financial services companies in America to serve everyday people from all walks of life.

Today, we’re part of an international holding company, with millions of customers and thousands of employees worldwide. Our insurance, retirement, and investment solutions help people make the most of what’s important to them.

We’re empowered by a vast agent network covering North America, with diversity to match. Together with our nonprofit research institute and foundation, we tune in, step up, and are a force for good — for our customers and the communities where we live, work, and play. United in our purpose, we help people create the financial freedom to live life on their terms.

What We Do

Transamerica is organized into three distinct businesses. These include 1) World Financial Group, including Transamerica Financial Advisors, 2) Protection Solutions and Savings & Investments, comprised of life insurance, annuities, employee benefits, retirement plans, and Transamerica Investment Solutions, and 3) Financial Assets, which includes legacy blocks of long term care, universal life, and variable and fixed annuities. These are supported by Transamerica Corporate, which includes Finance, People and Places, General Counsel, Risk, Internal Audit, Strategy and Development, and Corporate Affairs, which covers Communications, Brand, and Government and Policy Affairs.

Transamerica employs nearly 7,000 people. It’s part of Aegon, an integrated, diversified, international financial services group servingapproximately 23.9 million customersworldwide.* For more information, visit transamerica.com. 

Job Description Summary

Oversee indirect tax compliance and associated accounting. Responsible for overseeing staff as well as applying tax analysis, knowledge and judgment to activities that are diverse and complex.

Job Description

Responsibilities:

  • Extract financial data from various tax, accounting, and information systems to perform appropriate analyses.

  • Review indirect tax returns and associated tax accounting. Indirect tax responsibilities include, but are not limited to, state insurance premium tax, use tax, and franchise tax, as well as federal excise tax. Responsibilities may also include some research or analysis related to foreign value added tax (VAT), and any other non-income taxes.

  • Draft and/or review technical memos and outlines.

  • Develop non-standard reports and statements.

  • Lead assigned projects including integration of new tax laws and accounting principles. Research complicated tax law and accounting principles. Monitor tax law to ensure data integrity.

  • Perform special analysis and projects as requested.

  • Offer leadership and direction to others.

  • Assist in the evaluation of processes for operational efficiencies and effective risk management.

  • Utilize a thorough understanding of the business to proactively develop tax analysis and reports.

  • Work effectively with other departments/divisions to ensure business issues are resolved for the success of the company.

  • Responsible for adherence to the company's framework of internal controls.

  • May manage staff to achieve performance standards. Develop and motivate staff to achieve effectiveness through mentoring, training, and sharing knowledge. Ensure staff demonstrate appropriate customer service attitudes.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting or equivalent education/experience

  • Eight years of tax accounting experience

  • In-depth knowledge of assigned tax specialty

  • Analytical and critical thinking skills

  • Excellent communication skills

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment

  • Advanced computer skills

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Supervisory experience

Working Conditions:

  • Fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

  • Minimal to occasional travel may be required.

Compensation:

  • The Salary for this position generally ranges between $102,000 - $135,000 annually. Please note that the salary range is a good faith estimate for this position and actual starting pay is determined by several factors including qualifications, experience, geography, work location designation (in-office, hybrid, remote) and operational needs. Salary may vary above and below the stated amounts, as permitted by applicable law.

  • Additionally, this position is typically eligible for an Annual Bonus based on the Company Bonus Plan/Individual Performance and is at the Company’s discretion.

This job description is not a contract of employment nor for any specific job responsibilities. The Company may change, add to, remove, or revoke the terms of this job description at its discretion. Managers may assign other duties and responsibilities as needed. In the event an employee or applicant requests or requires an accommodation to perform job functions, the applicable HR Business Partner should be contacted to evaluate the accommodation request.

Disclaimer:
Beware of fake job offers!

We’ve been alerted to scammers impersonating Transamerica recruiters, particularly for remote positions. Please note:

  • We will never request personal information such as ID or payment for equipment upfront.

  • Official offers are sent via DocuSign following a verbal offer—not through text or email.

What We Offer

For eligible employees, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support both the personal and financial well-being of our employees.

Compensation Benefits

  • Competitive Pay

  • Bonus for Eligible Employees

Benefits Package

  • Pension Plan

  • 401k Match

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan

  • Tuition Reimbursement

  • Disability Insurance

  • Medical Insurance

  • Dental Insurance

  • Vision Insurance

  • Employee Discounts

  • Career Training & Development Opportunities

Health and Work/Life Balance Benefits

  • Paid Time Off starting at 160 hours annually for employees in their first year of service.

  • Ten (10) paid holidays per year (typically mirroring the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) holidays).

  • Be Well Company holistic wellness program, which includes Wellness Coaching and Reward Dollars

  • Parental Leave – fifteen (15) days of paid parental leave per calendar year to eligible employees with at least one year of service at the time of birth, placement of an adopted child, or placement of a foster care child.

  • Adoption Assistance

  • Employee Assistance Program

  • Back-Up Care Program

  • PTO for Volunteer Hours

  • Employee Matching Gifts Program

  • Employee Resource Groups

  • Inclusion and Diversity Programs

  • Employee Recognition Program

  • Referral Bonus Programs

Inclusion & Diversity 

 

We believe our commitment to diversity and inclusion creates a work environment filled with exceptional individuals. We’re thrilled to have been recognized for our efforts through the Human Rights Campaign Corporate Equality Index, Dave Thomas Adoption Friendly Advocate, and several Seramount lists, including the Inclusion Index, 100 Best Companies for Working Parents, Best Companies for Dads, and Top 75 Companies for Executive Women.

 

To foster a culture of inclusivity throughout our workforce, workplace, and marketplace, Transamerica offers a wide range of diversity and inclusion programs. This includes our company-sponsored, employee-driven Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), which are formed around a shared interest or a common characteristic of diversity. ERGs are open to all employees. They provide a supportive environment to help us better appreciate our similarities and differences and understand how they benefit us all.

  

Giving Back

About the Role

More Nutrition is investing in its International B2B business and is looking for an International Commercial Strategy Lead to take the brand's commercial playbook — developed centrally out of Germany — and adapt it into winning, market-specific plans across the UK, Benelux, Italy, Switzerland and Austria.

You will be the key point of contact between International country execution and Key Account Management (KAM) teams on one side, and the central commercial strategy function on the other — translating global priorities into local retailer and Amazon plans, and bringing local market realities back into global planning. You will report to the VP International, with a dotted line into the Global Commercial Lead.

Your mission

International Go-To-Market Strategy

  • Adapt the group's “Where to Play” trade-channel priorities and growth ambition for the UK, Benelux, Italy, Switzerland and Austria, in partnership with the global Brand Commercial team in Germany.
  • Localize the “How to Win” commercial strategy for each market: clear priorities, KPIs and customer-focused plans that reflect local retailer landscapes and competitive dynamics.

Commercial Fundamentals Across Markets

  • Assortment: define channel- and market-specific assortment (size, price and pack-format differentiation), hero SKUs and ranging recommendations for each priority retailer and Amazon; set and track distribution KPIs.
  • Place: partner with category management to define “perfect store” standards (shelf execution, secondary display, POS and claims) suited to local retail formats; set and track shelf and display KPIs.
  • Promotion: define local promotional guidelines (discount depth, frequency, mechanics) and in-store/online activation plans; track promotional ROI.
  • Price: define local omnichannel pricing and pack-size strategy, balanced against consumer value, competition, customer profitability and company margin; set and track pricing and margin KPIs.
  • People: enable local KAMs and field sales teams to execute with excellence, ensuring sell-in tools and brand/category training are delivered on time and in full.

Innovation & Sell-In

  • Localize the group's innovation masterplan and KAM/field-sales sell-in toolkits (prioritization, concept sell, execution visuals, store leave-behinds) for International retailers and Amazon.

Stakeholder & Operational Leadership

  • Act as the key point of contact between International country execution and KAM teams and the central/global commercial strategy function on day-to-day business and strategic planning.
  • Own commercial KPI and ROI tracking and reporting for International markets, and represent International in relevant global commercial review cadences.
  • Be the “voice” of International markets, feeding local retailer and consumer insight back into global brand and commercial planning.

Your experience & skills

  • 6–8 years of commercial strategy, trade marketing, category management or key account management within FMCG, CPG, sports/active nutrition or wellness.
  • Direct experience with major retailers in the UK and/or Benelux and possibly already a multi-market or regional experience.
  • Comfort working cross-functionally and cross-culturally with a German HQ team; German language skills are a plus but not required.
  • Strong analytical skills, with experience owning commercially relevant KPIs and turning data into action, combined with a hands-on, pragmatic mindset.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence across markets and functions without direct authority.
  • Based in the UK or the Netherlands, with willingness to travel regularly to Hamburg and across the International market cluster.

Why choose us?

Being part of our team means joining a high-performing company with a diverse and inclusive culture. In our fast-growing team of over 1,200 employees, we combine our passion for sports nutrition, supplements, and healthy foods with cutting-edge technology, production, and logistics processes. All of this serves one goal: providing our customers with top-quality products to support their healthy and active lifestyle.

You can look forward to a strong sense of team spirit, ongoing opportunities for professional growth and responsibility, and an exciting work environment that blends lifestyle and career. With locations in Hamburg, Elmshorn, Kaltenkirchen/Nützen, and Elsdorf, TQG offers diverse career opportunities in areas such as technology, product development, sales, marketing, and logistics. Additionally, you’ll benefit from:

  • Flexible working hours and remote work options
  • Workation
  • 28 days vacation/year
  • Attractive employee discounts

About Us

The Quality Group (TQG) is an innovative provider of sports nutrition products, bringing together the successful brands ESN and More Nutrition since 2021.

ESN has been the German market leader in sports nutrition since 2004, offering products like protein powders, bars, and supplements designed for ambitious fitness goals. Founded in 2017, More Nutrition focuses on healthy, reduced-sugar foods, providing solutions for conscious nutrition and weight management without compromise.

TQG’s vision is to help people become the best version of themselves. With passion and innovation, the company develops high-quality products that promote health, performance, and joy in life. Its agile company culture and exciting career opportunities make TQG a strong partner not only for customers but also for employees.

This is us – The Quality Group – nice to meet you! Now it’s your turn!
We look forward to your application! Regardless of gender, age, background, or identity – what matters to us is who you are and what you bring to the table. Join our team and grow with us!

Sales Engineer – ClinicalKey

Do you want to be the technical expert behind our flagship Clinical Decision Support platform?

About Elsevier Clinical Solutions

Clinical Solutions is the part of Elsevier Health that delivers evidence-based clinical decision support, drug information, and care guidance for hospitals, health systems, and individual clinicians. Our portfolio (including ClinicalKey, Elsevier Drug Information, Clinical Skills, Clinical Path and many others) is designed to sit inside existing clinical workflows and electronic health records and support decision making. Our products are underpinned by Elsevier's peer-reviewed medical content and a formal editorial governance process, so recommendations are current, sourced, and trustworthy. It is a strategically significant part of Elsevier with a clear remit: make trusted clinical evidence usable at the point of care. Join us!

About the Role

ClinicalKey surfaces evidence-based clinical answers in the electronic health record (EHR), grounded in evidence and with the context of the patient in front of the clinician. It is a sophisticated sale that spans clinical leadership, informatics, IT, security and AI governance. Our professional sales organization needs a technical partner they can bring into a deal and be joined at the hip to help our customers succeed.

As Sales Engineer, you will be that partner. You will own the technical narrative for how ClinicalKey integrates with the customer’s EHR, guide customers and their IT organizations through integration, security and AI review, and remove the technical barriers that stand between a strong clinical case and a signed agreement. You will work alongside ClinicalKey sellers across the North American market, and serve as the connective tissue between the field and our Product and Technology teams.

Responsibilities

  • Deal Support: Serve as the on-demand technical partner to ClinicalKey sellers. Join discovery calls, demonstrations and technical deep dives on request, and act as the single point of escalation for integration questions during an active sales cycle.
  • Technical Discovery: Qualify Patient Context fit early by assessing the customer’s environment: EHR vendor and version, FHIR API availability and release, SMART on FHIR launch support, single sign-on model, and which patient data elements are exposed.
  • Solution Demonstration: Deliver and tailor technical demonstrations that show ClinicalKey and Patient Context inside the customer’s clinical workflow, rather than a generic product tour.
  • Integration Expertise: Own the technical narrative for how the integration works – SMART on FHIR launch, patient context passing, OAuth 2.0 authorization, the FHIR resources consumed, and how retrieved content is grounded in the patient record.
  • Security and Compliance Review: Lead responses to customer security, privacy and compliance review, including data flow, PHI handling and retention, HIPAA and BAA questions, and third-party risk documentation, coordinating with Information Security and Legal as needed.
  • AI Governance: Represent the solution in AI governance and clinical informatics committee reviews, explaining model behavior, evidence sourcing, citation provenance and safeguards in terms that clinical and technical review boards will accept.
  • Scoping and Feasibility: Scope integration effort and prerequisites – customer IT resources, interface team involvement, environment access and vendor certification requirements – and set realistic expectations before commitments are made.
  • Pilots and Proofs of Concept: Design and run technical pilots, including success criteria, environment set-up and validation that the integration performs as expected in the customer’s environment.

  • Translation: Hold a credible conversation with an EHR analyst, a CIO and a practicing clinician in the same meeting, reframing the same integration for each audience.

Requirements

  • Have an understanding of clinical workflow and the ability to establish credibility with clinicians, informaticists and technical stakeholders alike.
  • Working knowledge of large language model-based solutions and the questions customers raise about accuracy, evidence and governance.
  • Deploy excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate technical detail into clinical and commercial value at any level of an organization.
  • Are proactive and able to work successfully in a matrixed environment, leading through demonstration, commitment and understanding of our marketplace.
  • Have project and time management skills with an ability to set and maintain priorities across multiple concurrent deals.
  • Able to bring energy and enthusiasm and foster effective teams.

Work in a Way That Works for You
We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organization. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance, and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals.

Working flexible hours - flexing the times when you work in the day to help you fit everything in and work when you are the most productive

Sphera is a leading global provider of enterprise software and services that enables companies to manage and optimize their environmental, health, safety and sustainability. Our mission is to create a safer, more sustainable and productive world.

Sphera is a portfolio company of Blackstone, a U.S.-based alternative asset investment company that focuses on private equity, technology and innovation, and more. Blackstone businesses succeed through strong partnerships, a personalized approach and a commitment to exceptional performance with uncompromising integrity. Sphera and Blackstone are leaders in the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) space.

We are guided by our core values of Customer Centricity, Accountability, Bias to Action, Innovation, and Collaboration. These values help us recruit the right talent to join our rapidly expanding team around the globe. It is important to us that each and every Spherion is not only eager to challenge themselves and knows how to get work done but is an awesome addition to our company culture.

POSITION SUMMARY

This role will be pivotal in advancing the company's mission of delivering secure, reliable, and innovative software solutions for U.S. government and DoD clients. The Cybersecurity Engineer serves as the resident security subject-matter expert embedded within the DevOps squad, owning the security compliance posture for software deployed in federal, DoD, and other highly regulated secure environments. The ideal candidate brings direct, hands-on experience operating within secure federal technology environments and a strong working knowledge of the security frameworks, tooling, and authorization processes that govern government-hosted systems. This individual will drive RMF/ATO lifecycle management, STIG implementation, vulnerability remediation, and DevSecOps integration across Sphera's product lines, ensuring that all systems maintain continuous compliance and readiness for deployment in secure government operating environments.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead cybersecurity for software deployed in secure federal and DoD environments, ensuring compliance with applicable government security policies, access requirements, and accreditation expectations.
  • Execute RMF activities, including system categorization, security control selection, implementation, assessment, and ATO documentation for federal or DoD-hosted systems.
  • Implement, configure, and validate STIGs across layers using DISA-approved or equivalent government security tooling.
  • Mitigate OWASP Top 10 and application-layer vulnerabilities across services.
  • Monitor security controls, scan vulnerabilities, and audit systems, producing reports and coordinating remediation with development and DevOps.
  • Manage POA&Ms, coordinating with government security stakeholders, ISSMs, and internal teams to track and resolve open findings.
  • Support FedRAMP and FISMA compliance, aligning controls with NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5.
  • Integrate security tooling and automated checks into CI/CD pipelines, advancing DevSecOps maturity.
  • Collaborate with engineers and the Principal Solutions Architect to conduct threat modeling, security design reviews, and application-level security assessments.
  • Maintain System Security Plans (SSPs), security architectures, and supporting ATO documentation packages in alignment with federal and DoD requirements.
  • Lead incident response activities for security events affecting systems deployed in secure government environments, coordinating with customer cybersecurity personnel and internal stakeholders.
  • Monitor SIEM alerts, analyze logs, and investigate anomalous activity.
  • Evaluate the security posture of third-party integrations, vendor tools, and emerging technologies for adoption in secure federal or DoD environments.
  • Embed security requirements into sprint planning, feature development, and release processes with the TPM, engineering squads, and product owners.
  • Stay informed on evolving federal, DoD, DISA, and agency-specific security policies, DISA guidance updates, and emerging threats, and proactively communicate their impact to the engineering organization.

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

  • U.S. citizen required; active DoD security clearance or ability to obtain and maintain one due to secure federal enclave access.
  • Minimum 3-5 years of hands-on cybersecurity experience in a federal, DoD or similarly regulated secure environments.
  • Strong working knowledge of secure federal or DoD environments, including segmented networks, access control, approved software baselines, and applicable security requirements.
  • Experience supporting or leading RMF processes, including ATO package preparation and submission for federal or DoD systems.
  • Proficiency in applying STIGs using DISA-approved tools (SCC, STIG Viewer, Nessus/ACAS) or comparable vulnerability and compliance platforms.
  • Solid understanding of FedRAMP Moderate and FISMA compliance, with ability to map security controls to NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5.
  • Experience with vulnerability management tools (e.g., Tenable.sc, Nessus, ACAS) in federal or DoD environments.
  • Familiarity with enterprise security tools including SIEM, IDS/IPS, and network security controls.
  • DevSecOps experience, including integrating SAST, DAST, and SCA scanning into CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps, Jenkins, or equivalent tools.
  • Familiarity with PKI, CAC/PIV authentication, and certificate management in federal or DoD environments.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills to translate complex security findings into actionable guidance for engineering teams and brief government stakeholders.
  • DoD 8570/8140 compliant certification at IAT Level II or higher (e.g., CompTIA Security+, CISSP, CEH, CAP, or equivalent).
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Experience working in segmented networks with an understanding of federal, DoD, or similarly regulated infrastructure and security requirements.

PROFESSIONAL SKILLS

  • Proven time management, organizational and follow-up skills to meet deadlines.
  • Work effectively, independently, and in a dynamic team environment.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills.
  • Must be willing to learn new technologies and processes as needed.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Secure Federal Environment Expertise

Strong working knowledge of secure federal, DoD, or similarly regulated operating environments, including security requirements, approval workflows, access constraints, and operational expectations — enabling the team to navigate complex government security landscapes with confidence and minimal disruption to delivery.

RMF and Compliance Execution

End-to-end ownership of RMF activities, from control implementation through ATO documentation, ensuring systems remain authorized and compliant throughout their lifecycle.

DevSecOps Integration

Embeds security as a continuous, automated discipline within engineering pipelines, reducing friction and shifting security left in the development lifecycle to maximize engineering velocity without sacrificing compliance.

Exceptional Stakeholder Communication and Collaboration

Foster strong partnerships by maintaining open, transparent, and effective communication with all stakeholders — including government program offices, ISSMs, and internal engineering teams — to ensure alignment and rapid resolution of security findings.

Incident Response and Threat Management

Rapid identification, escalation, and resolution of security events affecting systems deployed in secure government environments, with established protocols for coordinating with customer cybersecurity personnel.

Passion for Secure Innovation

Champion a security-first engineering culture that treats compliance not as a constraint but as a foundation for building reliable, mission-ready software for the DoD.

When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs. With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.

Job Title

Atomic Spectroscopy SME (REMOTE US or CAN)


Location(s)

US Remote - AL, US Remote - AL, US Remote - AR, US Remote - AZ, US Remote - CO, US Remote - CT, US Remote - DC, US Remote - DE, US Remote - FL, US Remote - GA, US Remote - IA, US Remote - ID, US Remote - IL, US Remote - IN, US Remote - KS, US Remote - KY, US Remote - LA, US Remote - MA, US Remote - MD, US Remote - ME, US Remote - MI, US Remote - MN, US Remote - MO, US Remote - MS, US Remote - MT {+ 25 more}

Job Description

The Senior Atomic Spectroscopy Support Specialist serves as a remote technical expert supporting PerkinElmer’s customers, field service engineers, and internal stakeholders throughout North America. This role is responsible for the rapid triage, diagnosis, and resolution of complex hardware, software, and application-related issues across supported atomic spectroscopy platforms.

Operating as part of the Technical Assistance Center (TAC), this position plays a critical role in maximizing customer instrument uptime, avoiding unnecessary field service visits, enabling first-time-fix outcomes, and delivering a consistently high-quality customer experience. The specialist applies deep technical knowledge, strong diagnostic reasoning, and the ability to visualize systems remotely—often without direct access to the instrument—to resolve known, repeat, and novel issues.

Location: This is a full-time remote position M-F and can be done either in US or CAN. Must be an Atomic Spectroscopy repair expert (5+ years).

Job Responsibilities:

  • Serve as a primary technical contact for incoming customer, field engineer, and internal support inquiries via phone and email for PerkinElmer Atomic Spectroscopy products. Triage requests ranging from basic product information to highly complex service and performance issues involving hardware, software, consumables, or methodology.
  • Perform detailed remote diagnostics of complex electro/mechanical equipment and computer/software systems by interpreting user descriptions, symptoms, error messages, system logs, and/or user generated data.
  • Drive issue resolution toward the most efficient and timely outcome: remote fix where possible, or a well-prepared service event where required. When remote resolution is achievable, guide customers or colleagues through corrective actions to restore performance and uptime.
  • When field service is required, determine likely root cause(s), recommend corrective actions, identify required parts, and document a clear plan of action to enable first-time-fix. If applicable to customer entitlement status, provide professional, accurate quotations for billable services and/or escalate leads for other PE products/services to appropriate internal teams.
  • Serve as a mentor and technical resource for colleagues by acting as liaison between global technical services, training teams, and the North American service organization to disseminate product updates, service notices, lessons learned, and other best practices.
  • Support operational excellence by adhering to documented procedures and maintaining accurate, complete, and timely service records. Ensure documentation quality enables effective handoffs, trend analysis, and timely escalation of emerging issues.
  • Participate in company offered training and development programs to support continuous improvement of technical expertise and soft skills. Training formats may include virtual or live classroom training, hands-on service location visits, field engineer shadowing, and travel as needed
  • Support additional cross-functional or special initiatives based on business needs as interest and workload allow. Contribute expertise in areas such as training/mentoring, SOP/documentation improvement, and/or data analysis.
  • Maintain training and compliance in areas of health and safety, security, environmental and operational aspects of daily activities in the working environment.

Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities of this job at any time.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Biology, Chemistry, Electronics, or related discipline
  • MUST have expert level experience with Atomic Spectroscopy Instrumentation on a repair level as a Subject Matter Expert (5+ years)
  • 5+ years' experience with at least two (2) of the following product technologies: AA, ICP-OES, ICP-MS
  • Role requires 5+ years of experience in a support, service, or an analytical laboratory environment performing duties of a product end user or service technician using atomic spectroscopy instrumentation.
  • Must be able to travel up to 25% for training (in the USA) and for quarterly field ride alongs.

Critical Skills:

  • Sound technical knowledge in all Atomic Spectroscopy product lines supported, including applications knowledge, and including proficiency in all software platforms of associated supported equipment.
  • Ability to apply sound judgment and critical‑thinking skills to complex technical problems, using structured, stepwise diagnostic reasoning and root‑cause analysis, with the ability to mentally model and visualize system behavior without direct access to guide effective remote troubleshooting and resolution.
  • Ability to safely and professionally execute technical work in accordance with written and verbal instructions, including interpreting technical bulletins and service manuals, working effectively under time constraints, maintaining focus and situational awareness, and adhering to universal precautions when working with potential electrical, chemical, radiologic, and biologic hazards.
  • Proficiency with standard computing tools to document work, analyze information, and generate reports, along with the ability to communicate complex technical information clearly and effectively with customers, peers, managers, and other technical support professionals.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ten (10) years experience in a support, service, or an analytical laboratory environment performing duties of a product end user or service technician using atomic spectroscopy instrumentation. Experience with all three (3) of the following product technologies: AA, ICP-OES, ICP-MS, is desired
  • Certification through company‑provided training on PerkinElmer instrumentation and software products, or equivalent hands‑on professional experience supporting PerkinElmer systems, is desired.

Working Environment:

  • Primary work environment is a home office or office based setting, supporting customers remotely via phone, email, and computer based systems for a majority of the role.
  • Work is primarily sedentary and computer focused, requiring extended periods of concentration, phone communication, and use of standard office equipment. Must be able to remain in a stationary position more than 25% of the time
  • Job pace may be fast moving, with periods of high workload depending on customer demand and escalations.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this position include without limitation, the ability to observe details at close range distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus in order to perform the essential service functions of this position.
  • Occasional travel may be required for training, team meetings, or visits to customer sites or company training facilities. During these activities, work may take place in laboratory or controlled environments requiring the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as lab coats and safety glasses.
  • When present in laboratory or service locations, the role may involve: 1) Moving between labs, corridors, and adjoining rooms, 2) Standing, bending, squatting, stretching, reaching, or working with instruments, tools, or controls, 3) Lifting or moving items typically up to 25 pounds, with infrequent lifting of heavier items as needed
  • Potential exposure to laboratory hazards including chemicals, biological materials, temperature extremes, or regulated waste may occur during training or site visits. All activities are performed in accordance with applicable health, safety, and environmental regulations.
  • Depending on assignment, employees may be required to complete medical clearance, respiratory protection training, and fit testing to support work in controlled environments during training or onsite activities.

The annual compensation range for this full-time position is $82,000 to $105,000 USD. The final base pay offered to the successful candidate will be determined by factors including internal equity, work location, as well as individual qualifications, such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

PerkinElmer is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability status, age, or veteran status or any other characteristics protected by applicable law. PerkinElmer is committed to a culturally diverse workforce.
